title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: HubSpot connector in the Researcher agent
summary: Hold: Microsoft's prerequisites page explicitly says connector grounding is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot and no extra charges apply, whereas the briefing treats that charge information as unpublished. The visibility rules also omit the individual-connector override in one passage, and the claims about specific HubSpot record types are not documented.

claims.claim: The HubSpot connector lets Researcher use third-party HubSpot information to enrich generated responses.
claims.quote: The HubSpot connector allows users using the Researcher agent to be able to leverage 3rd party information from HubSpot to enrich generated responses with relevant information.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the HubSpot connector is available by default on arrival.
claims.quote: Federated connectors are enabled by default for a tenant. ... When a Microsoft-published federated connector first appears in the admin center, it's available only to admins for seven calendar days before it's available to users.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket absence in the summary, Why it matters, Open questions and risk rationale with: 'Earlier preview documentation described federated connectors, including HubSpot, as enabled by default after a seven-calendar-day admin review window; the current overview instead describes availability through publisher-type, User access and connector settings.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/federated-connectors-overview. Retain defaultState unknown for the current arrival state rather than treating the historical preview default as a current commitment.

claims.claim: Microsoft-built federated connectors are available by default when the Microsoft publisher option is selected and the user is in User access.
claims.quote: Microsoft-built federated connectors are available by default when you select Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft in Agent and plugin access and include the user in User access.

claims.claim: External-publisher connectors require the external publisher option or individual admin enablement.
claims.quote: Connectors from external publishers are available only when you select Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers, or when an admin turns on the individual connector.

claims.claim: The current overview does not identify HubSpot's publisher type.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot federated connector Researcher default publisher seven calendar days contacts deals notes'; read current overview and preview search excerpts. Current gallery lists HubSpot without a publisher; preview text lists it under Microsoft-published connectors.
claims.fix: Narrow the open question to the current publisher classification and add: 'Earlier preview documentation listed HubSpot under Microsoft-published federated connectors.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/federated-connectors-overview.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Copilot accesses only source data the user already has permission to see.
claims.quote: Copilot only accesses data the user already has permission to see and makes changes the user is already permitted to make.

claims.claim: The HubSpot connector retrieves contacts into Researcher responses.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot Researcher connector contacts deals customer notes supported tools configuration'; read overview and release notes. Contact-table results describe Lakeflow Connect, not the Researcher federated connector.
claims.fix: Remove 'contacts' from the parenthetical list; the verified replacement for the whole sentence is 'Researcher can retrieve relevant HubSpot information through the connector, within the user's source-system permissions.'

claims.claim: The HubSpot connector retrieves deals into Researcher responses.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot Researcher connector contacts deals customer notes supported tools configuration'; read overview and release notes. Deal-table results concern Lakeflow Connect, not Researcher.
claims.fix: Remove 'deals' from the parenthetical list; use 'Researcher can retrieve relevant HubSpot information through the connector, within the user's source-system permissions.'

claims.claim: The HubSpot connector retrieves customer notes into Researcher responses.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot Researcher connector contacts deals customer notes supported tools configuration'; read overview and release notes. Neither specifies customer notes for this connector.
claims.fix: Remove 'customer notes' from the parenthetical list; use 'Researcher can retrieve relevant HubSpot information through the connector, within the user's source-system permissions.'

claims.claim: The connector can retrieve whatever the user can open in HubSpot.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot Researcher connector contacts deals customer notes supported tools configuration'; read overview and release notes. Source permissions bound access, but no text says the connector exposes every record the user can open.
claims.fix: Remove 'whatever the user can open in HubSpot'; use 'Researcher can retrieve relevant HubSpot information through the connector, within the user's source-system permissions.'

claims.claim: Federated connector settings and source permissions govern this live access rather than indexing settings.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center. ... Don't index external data into Microsoft 365. ... The source system enforces all permissions.

claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.claim: Federated connector communication is encrypted.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools are part of a connector and are not separately enabled.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Earlier preview documentation described a seven-calendar-day admin-only review window for Microsoft-published connectors.
claims.quote: When a Microsoft-published federated connector first appears in the admin center, it's available only to admins for seven calendar days before it's available to users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The currently fetched overview and management pages do not repeat the seven-day review window.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot federated connector Researcher default publisher seven calendar days contacts deals notes'; read complete current overview and management page. Seven-day text appears in preview search excerpts, not the current fetched pages.

claims.claim: The risk paragraph makes an allowed publisher type mandatory for visibility, although Scope allows individual enablement.
claims.quote: The connector's publisher type is allowed in Agent and plugin access, or an admin turned on the connector individually.
claims.fix: In Risk assessment: Change & support, replace 'only when its publisher type is allowed' with 'only when its publisher type is allowed or an admin has turned on the connector individually'. Keep the remaining enabled, User access, staged rollout and licence conditions.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Federated connectors require Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licensing or Microsoft 365 E7 for tenants and users.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.claim: Copilot Studio licences do not support federated Copilot connectors.
claims.quote: They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go does not support federated Copilot connectors.
claims.quote: They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: The prerequisites list a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence for every user who queries a federated source.
claims.quote: A Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license for every user who queries the federated source. For an eligibility matrix, see Licensing.

claims.claim: The HubSpot connector's entitlement model is add-on rather than included in the licence Copilot already needs.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on to Microsoft 365. If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Keep the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on or Microsoft 365 E7 requirement in licensing.notes, and add 'Connector grounding in Copilot is included for organisations with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences, and no extra charges apply' with https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/prerequisites.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate HubSpot-specific meter or numeric price.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot federated connector Copilot pricing meter Copilot Credits charge licensing'; read prerequisites, overview and billing search excerpts. No HubSpot-specific meter or numeric price found; prerequisites explicitly include connector grounding without extra charges.

claims.claim: A Copilot Credits rate specific to the HubSpot connector is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot federated connector Copilot pricing meter Copilot Credits charge licensing'; read prerequisites and billing-rate search excerpts. No HubSpot-specific Copilot Credits rate was found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether connector use carries an extra charge beyond the Copilot licence.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.
claims.fix: Replace the rationale's 'Microsoft Learn publishes no separate charge or meter for the HubSpot connector' with 'Microsoft says connector grounding in Copilot is included for organisations with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences and no extra charges apply'. State the same qualification in Cost and licensing and remove the open question about charges beyond that licence. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/prerequisites. The narrower absence of a HubSpot-specific numeric rate can remain.

claims.claim: The cited Microsoft pages do not state the cost of a HubSpot subscription.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot federated connector Copilot pricing meter Copilot Credits charge licensing'; read overview, prerequisites and release-note excerpts. These sources state no HubSpot subscription price.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Admins can audit federated connector activity in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The overview names Purview audit without providing an audit navigation path.
claims.quote: Searched: 'HubSpot Researcher connector Microsoft Purview audit activity path'; read full overview and audit search excerpts. Overview names Purview but provides no audit navigation path; returned connector-log guides concern Power Platform.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises reviewing connector capabilities and privacy terms against acceptable-use rules.
claims.quote: Before enabling or continuing to use a connector that exposes write, update, or delete tools, review the connector's capabilities, privacy terms, and third-party agreements against your organization's security, compliance, and acceptable-use requirements.
claims.fix: Remove 'as Microsoft advises for connectors' from the checklist item, leaving the review as the wiki's advice. Microsoft's stated recommendation is qualified to connectors exposing write, update or delete tools, while this Researcher experience is read-only.

claims.claim: Connector publishers can add or change tools over time.
claims.quote: The actions available through a connector depend on the tools exposed by the connector publisher. Publishers can add or change tools over time.

claims.claim: Some connectors expose an admin-centre tool view that administrators can review.
claims.quote: View a connector's tools in the admin center (Coming soon) ... For connectors that support this feature, the details page in the Microsoft 365 admin center includes a Tools section
claims.fix: Replace 'check the connector's tools in the admin centre where that view is available' with 'check the connector's tools in the admin centre where that view is available; Microsoft labels this admin tool view Coming soon'.

claims.claim: Users can turn off the source in Researcher.
claims.quote: Users can disable the data source at any time by turning off the source in Researcher or by managing the source in Copilot Chat settings.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to review Purview audit, but the controls table contains no audit row.
claims.quote: Review Microsoft Purview audit for connector activity; Microsoft says admins can audit federated connector activity there. ... The five controls rows cover publisher access, User access, enablement, staged rollout and blocking, not audit.
claims.fix: Remove the 'Review Microsoft Purview audit for connector activity' checklist bullet. Keep the verified statement about Purview auditing in Governance controls; do not add an unverified audit path or a new controls row.
